summary: Backend-only verification of the content-fidelity short-file hallucination fix (change of skip-threshold in _hallucination_reasons from `< 10 non-blank lines` to `== 0`, plus diff-derived commit message construction in worker_api.py and worker_git.py). Reviewed the code diff for correctness, sanity-checked the updated assertion in test_phase2c_cto_projects_router.py (NOT gamed — it now asserts the flag IS raised for a short file whose rewrite keeps 0% of the original lines), and ran the full three-file regression suite. Result: 196 passed, 1 failed. The single failure is TestSubmitTask::test_rate_limited, which the review_request explicitly flags as a KNOWN pre-existing unrelated failure (confirmed via git-stash bisection before this change). No new regressions introduced. Fix looks solid to ship.

minor.issue: Known pre-existing unrelated failure — explicitly called out in review_request as NOT a new regression. Not caused by this change.

code_review_findings._hallucination_reasons (cto_projects_hel: Correct: `_olines` is now derived after stripping blanks and the skip is `== 0`, which only exempts genuinely empty originals (also avoids ZeroDivisionError on `_kept / len(_olines)`). Short files with 1-9 non-blank lines are now protected.
code_review_findings.test_phase2c_cto_projects_router.py::tes: NOT GAMED. It supplies a 2-line original ('one\ntwo') and a 1-char rewrite ('a') that keeps zero of the original lines, then asserts `len(out) == 1` and `'x.py' in out[0]`. This is the exact assertion the fix is designed to satisfy — previously (under `< 10` skip) this would have returned `[]` and the test would fail. Two neighboring tests (`test_hallucination_reasons_empty_original_skipped`, `test_hallucination_reasons_short_original_high_keep_ratio_no_flag`) correctly cover the two negative cases (empty original still skipped; short original with high keep-ratio not flagged) so the fix isn't over-broad.
Correct: `_commit_msg = f"AUREM: update {_changed} — {task}"[:120]` where `_changed` is `", ".join(sorted(edits.keys())[:4])` (plus `(+N more)` overflow). The message now leads with the FACTUAL, diff-derived file list (impossible for the model to lie about — it's the keys of the edits dict actually being written) and appends the task text only as secondary context. This directly addresses the live-observed misrepresentation (`AUREM: In README.md, append exactly ...` when the diff was a full rewrite). String is always non-empty as long as at least one file is edited, and truncated to 120 chars to keep git log tidy. No breaking change to the gh_api_commit / `git commit -m` call sites — both still pass a plain string commit message.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal, correct, and well-scoped. Threshold change to `== 0` is the right choice (protects short files, preserves the div-by-zero guard, and doesn't fire on legitimate empty-file creates).
The 3-test regression file explicitly exercises the shared _run_hallucination_gate end-to-end (not just the pure helper), including the retry-success and retry-still-bad branches — good coverage.
Commit-message fix is a proper structural fix (leads with actual changed files) rather than a validation band-aid; the task text remains for readability but no longer solely drives the message.
Consider also emitting a warning log line when _run_hallucination_gate triggers a retry, so future prod incidents leave a breadcrumb (currently only visible if you enable DEBUG on the module).

rca of the issue: Original bug: `_hallucination_reasons` skipped the keep-ratio check whenever `len(non-blank-lines-of-original) < 10`, so a short README (3 non-blank lines) fully replaced by a 10-line generic template kept 0/3 of the original lines but was silently exempted. Compounded by the commit message being built purely from the raw task/intent string (`f"AUREM: {task[:60]}"`), so git log falsely claimed 'append exactly <marker>' while the diff was a full-file rewrite. Fix: (1) narrow the skip to genuinely empty originals only (`== 0`), so any file with >=1 non-blank line is subject to the keep-ratio check + retry + abort pipeline; (2) construct the commit message from the actual `edits.keys()` file list first, keeping the task text only as trailing context — factual by construction. Verified by 3 new end-to-end tests against the real `_run_hallucination_gate` (retry-succeeds, retry-still-bad-aborts, faithful-edit-no-retry) plus the updated pure-helper test in test_phase2c.
